title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X = Spec Z, x a closed point (more generally a finite set S of closed points), i: S -> X the closed immersion and U = X − S. M is a coefficient object, ideally a motivic sheaf. Grothendieck works with a hypothetical motivic hypercohomology ℍ^i(−, Q(n)), the 'Ext of motives', which he was trying to define at the time.

(1) Absolute purity. For the codimension-1 regular point x he writes i_x^! M = i_x^* M(−1)[−2]. This is the Gysin isomorphism, the analogue of i^! Z_ℓ(n) = Z_ℓ(n−1)[−2] in étale cohomology.

(2) Localization. The triangle i_* i^! M -> M -> Rj_* j^* M gives the long exact sequence
… -> H^{i−2}(S, i^*M(−1)) -> H^i(X,M) -> H^i(U,M) -> H^{i−1}(S, i^*M(−1)) -> …

(3) Input from the previous page. The cohomology of a finite field F_q is that of π = Ẑ, generated by Frobenius, so it lives only in degrees 0 and 1. Hence H^i(X,M) ≅ H^i(U,M) for i ≠ 1,2,3. In low degrees one gets
0 -> H^1(X) -> H^1(U) -> H^0(S, i^*M(−1)) -> H^2(X) -> H^2(U) -> H^1(S, i^*M(−1)) -> H^3(X) -> H^3(U) -> 0.
He adds the query 'H^3(U,M) = 0 ?'. A marginal note says that for motives, or for i ≥ 4, both sides should vanish.

(4) Coefficients M = Q(n). Then i^*M(−1) = Q(n−1)_S. The previous page records:
- ℍ^i(F_q, Q(m)) = 0 for m ≠ 0;
- ℍ^0(F_q, Q) = ℍ^1(F_q, Q) = Q.
This is a Weil-group normalisation: the Z-lattice in H^1 is generated by Frobenius, so ℍ^1(F_q, Z) = Z. Consequences:
- If n ≠ 1, then H^i(X, Q(n)) ≅ H^i(U, Q(n)) for all i, marked '[est-ce vrai ??]'.
- If n = 1, the sequence is 0 -> H^1(X,Q(1)) -> H^1(U,Q(1)) -> Q^S -> H^2(X,Q(1)) -> H^2(U,Q(1)) -> Q^S -> H^3(X,Q(1)) -> 0.

(5) Reading of the n = 1 sequence. H^1(−, Q(1)) = O^*⊗Q, which is 0 for Z and Q^S for Z[1/S]; the map to Q^S is the valuation map, an isomorphism. H^2(−, Q(1)) ⊇ Pic⊗Q = 0. So H^2(X, Q(1)) = 0, provided H^2 contains nothing beyond Pic⊗Q.

The last map Q^S -> H^3(X, Q(1)) is surjective. If H^2(U, Q(1)) is the kernel of the sum map Q^S -> Q, this is an integral/Weil analogue of the Brauer reciprocity sequence Br(Z[1/S]) -> ⊕ Q/Z -> Q/Z. Then H^3(X, Q(1)) = Q via the sum ('trace').

He concludes: H^i(X, Q(1)) = 0 except for i = 3, where it is a quotient of Q-type ('… de Q !'). This consistency-checks the previous page's claims ℍ^i(Spec Z, Z(1)) = Z for i = 3 (0 otherwise) and ℍ^i(Spec Z, Z) = Z for i = 0 (0 otherwise). Those claims amount to a 3-dimensional Poincaré-type duality for Spec Z with integral coefficients, Z(1) dualizing and an integral trace H^3(Z(1)) -> Z.

Purpose: to compute the motivic cohomology of Spec Z and test whether it has a 3-manifold-like duality with integral, not torsion, coefficients.
errors: The archimedean place is ignored. 'Spec Z' is treated as if compact; in the later Weil-étale theory the clean duality H^3 = Z requires the compactification \bar{Spec Z} (or compact supports), and the regulator/archimedean contributions alter H^1, H^2 for n = 1.

With genuine (Voevodsky/Bloch) motivic cohomology, H^1(F_q, Q(0)) = 0, not Q. So the n = 1 computation holds only for a Weil-étale-type theory, where Frobenius gives an H^1. In ordinary motivic cohomology H^3(Spec Z, Q(1)) = 0. The statement 'H^3 ≠ 0' is thus theory-dependent, which Grothendieck does not flag.
The step H^2(X, Q(1)) = 0 and the description of H^3 rest on unverified assumptions about H^2(U, Q(1)) (Brauer-type part) and on H^3(U) = 0, which is itself queried. The conclusion is heuristic.

The n ≠ 1 claim is marked '[est-ce vrai ??]'. It is correct rationally, by Quillen's computation of K-theory of finite fields plus the localization sequence (K_{2n-1}(Z)⊗Q ≅ K_{2n-1}(Z[1/S])⊗Q). It is not proved here.

ideas.what: Purity i^!M = i^*M(−1)[−2] for a closed point of Spec Z in a motivic coefficient theory
ideas.modern_name: Absolute purity / Gysin isomorphism for motivic sheaves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 4/5 conjecture); proved étale by Gabber, motivic by Cisinski–Déglise

ideas.what: Localization long exact sequence for X = Spec Z, U open, S finite set of primes, in motivic cohomology with Q(n) coefficients
ideas.modern_name: Localization sequence for motivic cohomology / K-theory (Quillen localization)

ideas.what: Rational motivic cohomology of Spec Z unchanged by removing primes when weight n ≠ 1
ideas.modern_name: Rational invariance of K_{2n−1}⊗Q under localization (finite-field K-groups are torsion)

ideas.what: Using H^1(F_q, Q) = Q (Frobenius-generated, Weil normalisation) to obtain a nonzero H^3(Spec Z, Q(1)) and integral trace H^3(Spec Z, Z(1)) = Z
ideas.modern_name: Weil-étale cohomology and its duality RΓ_W(Spec Z̄, Z(1)) -> Z[−3]

ideas.what: Spec Z as a 3-dimensional object with Poincaré-type duality (H^0(Z) = Z dual to H^3(Z(1)) = Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mazur (1963–64), Artin–Verdier; later Kapranov, Reznikov, Morishita

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a motivic cohomology of Spec Z whose finite-field stalks have a Weil-type H^1 = Q (Z), and derives a nonzero integral class in H^3(Spec Z, Z(1)) acting as a trace. This anticipates Lichtenbaum's Weil-étale cohomology and the Flach–Morin duality with dualizing object Z(1)[3] for Spec Z̄, which are usually dated to ~1998–2018 and not linked to Grothendieck.
missed.quote: H^i(X,Q(1)) = 0 sauf pour i=3, où c'est un[?] facteur[?] de Q !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents an early, possibly 1965, Grothendieck origin for the 'integral Artin–Verdier / Weil-étale' picture of Spec Z as a compact 3-manifold with integral Poincaré duality. That is relevant to the history of Lichtenbaum's program and of arithmetic topology.

missed.claim: He leaves open whether H^3(U, Q(1)) vanishes and whether the n ≠ 1 localization isomorphism holds, and he omits the archimedean place. Completing the computation within a Weil-type theory forces compactification at infinity, which is exactly where Lichtenbaum and Flach–Morin later had to work.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mostly resolved in modern Weil-étale theory. Historically it shows which point Grothendieck identified as unclear.

deep.surprise_reason: The localization computation itself is routine. Combined with the previous page, though, it shows Grothendieck positing a motivic cohomology of Spec Z with Frobenius-generated H^1 of finite fields and integral duality H^3(Spec Z, Z(1)) = Z. That is a Weil-étale-style picture usually credited to Lichtenbaum decades later. The content is speculative, the date is uncertain (1965 to c.1977), and it ignores the archimedean place, so the surprise is moderate.
transcription_corrections: Line 'M = [-Z-]Q(n)': the struck symbol looks like a blackboard Z overwritten by Q; reading M = Q(n) is fine.
'pour des motifs[?], ou si i ≥ 4, les deux membres devraient être = 0': the first word may be 'pour des motifs' or 'pour des raisons'; uncertain.
The marginal '[-H_x-]' after i_x^*(M) is a struck-out symbol; intended statement is i_x^*(M)(−1) restricted to S equals Q(n−1)_S.
Final line plausibly reads 'H^i(X,Q(1)) = 0 sauf pour i = 3, où c'est un quotient de Q !' (or 'quotient de Q^S'); 'facteur' is a doubtful reading.
The struck subscript in 'Q_[S](n)' is a deleted S.
